# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

Quillstone Payments is a privately held financial-services company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Hamburg. It builds payment and money-management tools for small merchants, including payment terminals, a point-of-sale app and a business account; it has also introduced a personal account for merchants’ customers. The company serves a few million merchants across Europe and the Americas and employs around 2,500 people across roughly 20 offices. Its machine-learning team works on customer-support automation and fraud models.

Quillstone’s culture emphasizes ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes. Teams have autonomy to solve merchant problems, guided by shared values rather than heavy processes. The company also values pragmatism, humility, candid feedback and open sharing of context. It is office-first, with some team-agreed flexibility, and supports development through training budgets, peer feedback, internal tech talks and twice-yearly development-plan reviews. Quillstone also supports local business education projects and publishes an annual inclusion report.

Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I bring six years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than four years as a data scientist, building machine-learning models and practical data workflows used by operational and growth teams. Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get quick, low-friction support particularly interests me, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my applied modelling and production-data experience to that work.

At Thistlebox, I developed a weekly LightGBM demand-forecasting model for orders by recipe and region, forecasting up to six weeks ahead. Feature engineering for calendar, price and menu-position factors helped reduce WAPE from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I implemented a scheduled workflow in Vertex AI Workbench that writes forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker. I also built an XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery to target retention offers; a 10% holdout validation found churn decreased by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.

Alongside modelling, I design and analyse around 40 A/B tests each year and built a Python and Streamlit sequential-testing calculator with Docker, now used by around 25 colleagues. The data platform team handles its deployment on Cloud Run. I also write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models. These experiences have taught me to connect model development with the workflows and decisions that make it useful, while working across teams and communicating results to leadership.

I hold an MSc in Statistics with distinction and bring a strong foundation in Python, statistical modelling and feature engineering, as well as hands-on experience with GCP data workflows. I would be glad to discuss how this background could support Quillstone’s work on AI systems for customer operations and merchant support. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
